candidates.attacker_control: The `input` argument of getValidDirectoryPath()/isValidDirectoryPath()/assertValidFileUpload() is user input the application is validating (e.g. a request parameter selecting an upload/save/browse directory). The `parent` argument is the application's trusted base directory and is not attacker-controlled; the chosen sibling path is.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Verified that '..'-based traversal and symlink escapes are blocked by getCanonicalPath() (the startsWith check then fails), leaving the prefix-sibling case as the residual bypass. Verified 465-469 do not re-enforce containment (they only require canonical == raw input and regex compliance; the regex in configuration/esapi/ESAPI.properties and src/test/resources/esapi/ESAPI.properties permits '/', letters, digits, '-', etc.). Checked the sibling file-name method (getValidFileName) and could not construct a traversal there. Considered that a pre-existing prefix-sharing directory (not arbitrary traversal) is required, which narrows exploitability.
candidates.impact: Bypass of a path-containment validation control in a security library: an attacker-influenced path outside the intended parent directory is validated and returned as safe, so applications that read, write, list, or upload into the returned directory can be steered outside the intended sandbox (path traversal / directory escape), e.g. into a sibling directory (web-served or backup directory) that shares the parent's name prefix. The bypass uses no '..' and no symlinks, so canonicalization-based defenses do not catch it.
candidates.prerequisites: 1) An application calls Validator.getValidDirectoryPath(context, userInput, trustedParent, ...) and trusts the result to be confined to trustedParent. 2) A directory already exists whose canonical path starts with trustedParent's canonical path but is not a separator-delimited descendant (e.g. /base/uploads vs /base/uploads-old, /base/uploads2). 3) The supplied path contains no percent/HTML-entity sequences, because line 466 canonicalizes it and line 467 requires it to equal the raw input.
candidates.root_cause: The 'directory inside parent' control is `!dir.getCanonicalPath().startsWith(parent.getCanonicalPath())` (DefaultValidator.java:460). A String prefix comparison with no trailing File.separator (or Path.startsWith) boundary accepts any existing directory whose canonical path merely begins with the parent's canonical path, i.e. siblings such as `/srv/app/uploads-evil` for parent `/srv/app/uploads`. The later checks (canonical path must equal the raw input at 465-469 and satisfy the generic DirectoryName regex) do not re-validate containment, so the out-of-parent value is returned to the caller. This contradicts the documented guarantee in Validator.java:246-247 ('existing subdirectory (at any level) of the specified parent').
candidates.title: DefaultValidator.getValidDirectoryPath() containment check bypassable via path-prefix sibling directory (CWE-22/CWE-697)
candidates.trace: Caller -> Validator.getValidDirectoryPath(context, input, parent, allowNull) -> DefaultValidator.getValidDirectoryPath: (a) 448-453 require the input path to exist and be a directory; (b) 454-459 verify parent exists/is a directory; (c) 460 is the only containment check: for input='/srv/app/uploads-evil' and parent='/srv/app/uploads', the canonical paths are '/srv/app/uploads-evil' and '/srv/app/uploads', and startsWith() returns true, so no ValidationException is thrown; (d) 465-469 only canonicalize the path against the generic DirectoryName regex (letters, digits, '-', '/', etc.) and require canonical.equals(input), which the attacker-chosen input satisfies; (e) 470 returns the out-of-parent path as valid. Appending File.separator to the parent (or using java.nio.file.Path.startsWith) would reject this input.
candidates.unverified: No code/tests were executed; the bypass is shown by source reasoning only. Whether this is the dataset's target and whether upstream later fixed this check are unverified. No caller of getValidDirectoryPath with attacker-controlled input exists in this repository (it is a framework API for application callers), so reachability is caller-dependent. Windows/macOS case-insensitivity and container/OS normalization variants were not tested.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22 Path Traversal (containment-check bypass / incorrect string comparison)

summary: Reviewed the assigned ESAPI (esapi-java-legacy, pom 2.1.0.1-SNAPSHOT) snapshot as a defensive source review. I inspected the validator, HTTP utilities, servlet wrappers/filters, authenticator/user code, crypto (JavaEncryptor, CipherText/Serializer, CryptoHelper, KDF, CryptoToken), codecs/encoder, WAF rules/parser, new configuration loaders, access control, JSP tags, the related tests, and ESAPI.properties defaults. Most controls are defensively implemented (upload filename validation canonicalizes before matching and requires raw input == canonical base name; redirects/headers/cookies are validated; MAC is checked before decryption; Base64 deserialization is gated by a system property). The strongest source-verifiable lead is a containment-check flaw in DefaultValidator.getValidDirectoryPath(): the parent check is a plain String.startsWith() prefix compare with no separator boundary, so an existing sibling directory whose path starts with the parent path (e.g. /srv/app/uploads-evil vs parent /srv/app/uploads) is validated as inside the parent, contradicting the documented contract. No code or tests were executed; this is a lead, not a runtime-confirmed vulnerability.
